protocol.py: 4 biology problems (3 warnings, 1 note).

1. WARNING CONTAM-WELL: A used tip carried master mix (tube A1 in slot 3), the liquid from
tube B1 in slot 3, the liquid from tube C1 in slot 3, the liquid from tube D1 in slot 3 and
4 more into 25 wells it was never meant for
   line 68:  p300_multi.dispense(23, well)
   At line 68 the tip touched the liquid in wells B4, B7, B10, C1, C4, C7, C10, E1 and 17
   more in slot 7 while it still carried master mix (tube A1 in slot 3), the liquid from
   tube B1 in slot 3, the liquid from tube C1 in slot 3, the liquid from tube D1 in slot 3
   and 4 more from an earlier step (this line did it 14 times). A tip that has touched one
   liquid leaves a little of it in the next liquid it touches. The protocol never transfers
   that liquid into these wells on purpose, so it was not meant to be there. If the wells
   hold different samples, each now holds a little of another.
   Affected: wells B4, B7, B10, C1, C4, C7, C10, E1 and 17 more in slot 7.
   Fix: Use a fresh tip for each well at line 68. If one tip must serve many wells, dispense
   from above the liquid (for example `well.top()`) so that the tip never touches what is
   already in the well.
   Source: Lab Manager: minimizing cross-contamination in automated liquid handling
           https://www.labmanager.com/minimizing-cross-contamination-in-automated-liquid-handling-workflows-35194
   [8ed93ba51a90]

2. WARNING WELL-CAPACITY: More liquid than the well is rated for: 117 ul against 100 ul, 4
wells
   line 68:  p300_multi.dispense(23, well)
   At line 68 the robot filled wells E2, E5, E8 and E11 in slot 7 past the 100 ul the maker
   states for it (this line did it 4 times), reaching 117 ul, under the 217 ul the well
   holds to its rim. Above the stated maximum the liquid climbs the wall and wets the seal,
   a tip going in displaces it over the edge, and the volumes still add up on paper, so the
   plate map does not see it and the simulator says nothing. Wells: wells E2, E5, E8 and E11
   in slot 7.
   Affected: wells E2, E5, E8 and E11 in slot 7.
   Fix: Use labware rated for the volume, or scale every volume down so the fullest well
   stays under the stated maximum with room to mix.
   Source: Opentrons labware schema 2: totalLiquidVolume, the total well volume in
   microlitres
           https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Opentrons/opentrons/edge/shared-data/labware/schemas/2.json
   Source: Bartley et al. 2023, LabOP: a protocol never adds more liquid than its container
   holds
           https://jakebeal.github.io/Publications/JETC23-LabOP.pdf
   [40090fe73652]

3. WARNING UNMIXED-AT-END: 12 wells never mixed after sample 1, sample 7, sample 13, sample
19 and 8 more went in (2 to 8% of the well)
   line 77:  p20_single.dispense(2, dst_well)
   At line 77 the robot added sample 1, sample 7, sample 13, sample 19 and 8 more to wells
   A1, B1, C1, D1, E1, E2, F1, F2 and 4 more in slot 7, which already held master mix,
   water, the liquid from tube B1 in slot 3, the liquid from tube B1 in slot 4 and 4 more
   (this line did it 12 times). The addition was 2 to 8% of the well, nothing mixed the well
   afterwards, and the run ended with them that way. Two liquids layered in a small well do
   not mix on their own, so what the well holds is not at the concentration you calculated.
   The liquid added last is a sample, so nothing else in the workflow will mix it: a
   normalisation or a pool left like this is not what it says it is.
   Affected: wells A1, B1, C1, D1, E1, E2, F1, F2 and 4 more in slot 7.
   Fix: Mix wells A1, B1, C1, D1, E1, E2, F1, F2 and 4 more in slot 7 after line 77:
   `mix_after=(5, 20 to 94)` on the transfer, or `pipette.mix(5, 20 to 94, well)`, with the
   volume about 80% of what the well holds.
   Source: Artel: automated liquid handlers as sources of error
           https://www.bioprocessintl.com/assays/automated-liquid-handlers-as-sources-of-error
   Source: Illumina: normalising library concentrations (pipette up and down 10 times to
   mix)
           https://support.illumina.com/ko-kr/bulletins/2017/03/best-practices-for-manually-normalizing-library-concentrations.html
   Source: Thermo PowerTrack user guide (a reaction plate not mixed well gives variable
   replicates)
           https://documents.thermofisher.com/TFS-Assets/LSG/manuals/MAN0018825_PowerTrackSYBRGreenMasterMix_UG.pdf
   Source: Integra: how to perform serial dilutions
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/global/en/applicationguide/master-art-pipetting-and-learn-how-perform-serial-dilutions-our-comprehensive-guide
   [ed249b9f83b6]

4. NOTE UNMIXED-AT-END: 5 wells never mixed after the liquid from tube C1 in slot 3, the
liquid from tube C1 in slot 4, the liquid from tube D1 in slot 3 and the liquid from tube D1
in slot 4 went in (25% of the well)
   line 68:  p300_multi.dispense(23, well)
   At line 68 the robot added the liquid from tube C1 in slot 3, the liquid from tube C1 in
   slot 4, the liquid from tube D1 in slot 3 and the liquid from tube D1 in slot 4 to wells
   F8, F11, G5, G8 and G11 in slot 7, which already held master mix, water, the liquid from
   tube B1 in slot 3 and the liquid from tube B1 in slot 4 (this line did it 5 times). The
   addition was 25% of the well, nothing mixed the well afterwards, and the run ended with
   them that way. Two liquids layered in a small well do not mix on their own, so what the
   well holds is not at the concentration you calculated. If the plate is vortexed and spun
   down before it is used, nothing is wrong; if it goes straight to the instrument, the
   wells are not what the protocol says they are.
   Affected: wells F8, F11, G5, G8 and G11 in slot 7.
   Fix: Mix wells F8, F11, G5, G8 and G11 in slot 7 after line 68: `mix_after=(5, 74)` on
   the transfer, or `pipette.mix(5, 74, well)`, with the volume about 80% of what the well
   holds.
   Source: Artel: automated liquid handlers as sources of error
           https://www.bioprocessintl.com/assays/automated-liquid-handlers-as-sources-of-error

   mix)

The Opentrons simulator (8.8.2) passed this protocol with no error: it checks that the robot
can make the moves, not what they do to the liquids.

findings.title: A used tip carried master mix (tube A1 in slot 3), the liquid from tube B1 in slot 3, the liquid from tube C1 in slot 3, the liquid from tube D1 in slot 3 and 4 more into 25 wells it was never meant for
findings.explanation: At line 68 the tip touched the liquid in wells B4, B7, B10, C1, C4, C7, C10, E1 and 17 more in slot 7 while it still carried master mix (tube A1 in slot 3), the liquid from tube B1 in slot 3, the liquid from tube C1 in slot 3, the liquid from tube D1 in slot 3 and 4 more from an earlier step (this line did it 14 times). A tip that has touched one liquid leaves a little of it in the next liquid it touches. The protocol never transfers that liquid into these wells on purpose, so it was not meant to be there. If the wells hold different samples, each now holds a little of another.
findings.fix: Use a fresh tip for each well at line 68. If one tip must serve many wells, dispense from above the liquid (for example `well.top()`) so that the tip never touches what is already in the well.

findings.title: More liquid than the well is rated for: 117 ul against 100 ul, 4 wells
findings.explanation: At line 68 the robot filled wells E2, E5, E8 and E11 in slot 7 past the 100 ul the maker states for it (this line did it 4 times), reaching 117 ul, under the 217 ul the well holds to its rim. Above the stated maximum the liquid climbs the wall and wets the seal, a tip going in displaces it over the edge, and the volumes still add up on paper, so the plate map does not see it and the simulator says nothing. Wells: wells E2, E5, E8 and E11 in slot 7.
findings.fix: Use labware rated for the volume, or scale every volume down so the fullest well stays under the stated maximum with room to mix.

findings.title: 12 wells never mixed after sample 1, sample 7, sample 13, sample 19 and 8 more went in (2 to 8% of the well)
findings.explanation: At line 77 the robot added sample 1, sample 7, sample 13, sample 19 and 8 more to wells A1, B1, C1, D1, E1, E2, F1, F2 and 4 more in slot 7, which already held master mix, water, the liquid from tube B1 in slot 3, the liquid from tube B1 in slot 4 and 4 more (this line did it 12 times). The addition was 2 to 8% of the well, nothing mixed the well afterwards, and the run ended with them that way. Two liquids layered in a small well do not mix on their own, so what the well holds is not at the concentration you calculated. The liquid added last is a sample, so nothing else in the workflow will mix it: a normalisation or a pool left like this is not what it says it is.
findings.fix: Mix wells A1, B1, C1, D1, E1, E2, F1, F2 and 4 more in slot 7 after line 77: `mix_after=(5, 20 to 94)` on the transfer, or `pipette.mix(5, 20 to 94, well)`, with the volume about 80% of what the well holds.

findings.title: 5 wells never mixed after the liquid from tube C1 in slot 3, the liquid from tube C1 in slot 4, the liquid from tube D1 in slot 3 and the liquid from tube D1 in slot 4 went in (25% of the well)
findings.explanation: At line 68 the robot added the liquid from tube C1 in slot 3, the liquid from tube C1 in slot 4, the liquid from tube D1 in slot 3 and the liquid from tube D1 in slot 4 to wells F8, F11, G5, G8 and G11 in slot 7, which already held master mix, water, the liquid from tube B1 in slot 3 and the liquid from tube B1 in slot 4 (this line did it 5 times). The addition was 25% of the well, nothing mixed the well afterwards, and the run ended with them that way. Two liquids layered in a small well do not mix on their own, so what the well holds is not at the concentration you calculated. If the plate is vortexed and spun down before it is used, nothing is wrong; if it goes straight to the instrument, the wells are not what the protocol says they are.
findings.fix: Mix wells F8, F11, G5, G8 and G11 in slot 7 after line 68: `mix_after=(5, 74)` on the transfer, or `pipette.mix(5, 74, well)`, with the volume about 80% of what the well holds.
